RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, August 23, 2011/Bhadra 1, 1933 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Drinking Water and Sanitation; Environment and Forests;
Finance; Health and Family Welfare; Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises;
Petroleum and Natural Gas; Rural Development)
Total number of questions — 20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Regulatory Framework for MFIs
*281. SHRI R.C. SINGH: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) the reason for not providing a
regulatory framework to deal with the
various issues relating to Micro Finance
Institutions (MFIs);
(b) whether Malegam Committee
constituted by the Reserve Bank of India
has also recommended  setting up of a
regulator;
(c) whether Government would
consider fixing a cap on lending rate of MFI,
as a stop-gap arrangement in view of the
problems being faced by poor people;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Supply of LLINs to Gujarat for the
Malaria Control Project
*282. SHRI KANJIBHAI PA TEL: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has any plan
to supply Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets
(LLINs) to Gujarat under the proposed
World Bank-assisted Malaria Control
Project, during 2011-12;
(b) if so, the number of LLINs proposed
to be supplied to Gujarat during 2011-12;
and
(c) if supply of LLINs is not proposed
during 2011-12, then the  probable  date  of
its supply?
Distribution of expired medicines
under NRHM
†*283. SHRI KAPTAN SINGH
SOLANKI: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that expired
medicines are being distributed to people
under  the National Rural Health Mission
(NRHM) being run by Government;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the amount spent by Government
on this Scheme till date, State-wise?

86
Setting up of Y oga OPDs in hospitals
*284. SHRI A.A. JINNAH: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
set up Yoga OPDs in any Government or
private hospitals in the States of Punjab,
Haryana and Rajasthan; and
(b) if so, the details thereof, indicating
the interest shown by any of the State
Governments in this regard?
Impact of decontrolled pricing regime
on common man
*285. SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is  a fact that the cost of
petroleum products has shot up several
times in the past few months;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
docontrolled regime of petroleum products
has resulted in greater burden on the
common man; and
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government
so that the decontrolled pricing regime of
petroleum products do not harm the
common man's family budget?
Study on impact of mines on ecology
and environment of Goa
*286. SHRI SHANTARAM NAIK:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of iron ore mines in
operation in Goa;
(b) the number of mines stopped from
operating, if any;
(c) the number of applications for
operating mines in Goa pending with the
Ministry;
(d) whether the Ministry has made
study of ecological/environmental impact
of mines operating in Goa; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Delay in starting proposed AIIMS-like
institutions
*287. SHRI A. ELAV ARASAN: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the six proposed AIIMS-
like institutions remain unborn even seven
years after their conception;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it took six years to start the
work even after detailed project report was
cleared by Government and the revised
estimate for each institution has more than
doubled;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the steps taken by Government for
speedy completion of  the works to make
these institutions operational at  an early
date?
Black carbon in the ambit of UN
framework convention
†*288. DR. RAM PRAKASH: Will the
Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether a developing country like
India has now accepted bringing of black
carbon within the ambit of United Nations
Framework Convention, a unit of United
Nations, despite its opposition to it earlier;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

87
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) if not, the present status thereof
vis-a-vis India?
Launching  of the National Rural
Housing and Habitat Policy
*289. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is planning to launch the National Rural
Housing and Habitat Policy;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
amount provided under the Indira Awas
Yojana (IAY) is still insufficient for the
village poor to replace their temporary
structures with a permanent dwellings; and
(d) if  so,  the  steps  being  taken
for  providing  more  funds  under  this
Scheme?
Status of PMGSY in different States
of the country
†*290. SHRI RAGHUNANDAN
SHARMA: Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of phases of the Pradhan
Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)
completed in the country, State-wise;
(b) the names of the States which are
lagging behind in road construction and the
time by when they will achieve the targets;
(c) the names of States where the
construction work of next phase under the
Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana has
been stalled; and
(d) the reasons therefor?
Immunization for children
*291. DR. JANARDHAN
WAGHMARE : Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
more than 55 per cent of children in the age
group of 0-2 years do not receive
comprehensive immunization in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether due to lack of facilities  for
immunization of children, they either die
or suffer from major diseases; and
(d) if so, the  steps taken by the Central
Government, in consultation with the State
Governments, to protect children from
various diseases?
Vigilance and monitoring committees
under MGNREGS
*292. SHRI PRA VEEN RASHTRAPAL:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry had issued
instructions from time to time and
appointed Members of Parliament on the
State level vigilance and monitoring
committees under the Mahatma Gandhi
National Rural Employment Guarantee
Scheme (MGNREGS);
(b) whether the Ministry is aware that
the State Government of Gujarat has not
arranged any such meeting of the vigilance
and monitoring committee from 2006 to
March 2011; and
(c) if so, the details of action being taken
by the Ministry in such matters where State
Governments could not arrange quarterly
meetings of the vigilance and monitoring
committees?

88
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Curtailment in SKO allocation to
Gujarat
*293. SHRI NATUJI HALAJI
THAKOR: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has curtailed  by 32 per  cent the allocation
quota for PDS Superior Kerosene Oil
(SKO) for Gujarat from June, 2011,
without any specific reasons, against the
monthly allocation of 76710 Ltrs. till May,
2011;
(b) if so, the details of allocation of SKO
to other States during 2010-11 and
2011-12, State-wise;
(c) the adverse impact of this decision
on 84 lakh non-LPG-PDS card holders in
the State;
(d) the per capita availability of SKO
during 2010-11 and 2011-12, State-wise;
and
(e) the reasons for variation in per
capita availability of PDS-SKO in various
States?
Misuse of the Land Acquisition Act in
Haryana
*294. SARDAR SUKHDEV SINGH
DHINDSA: Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has received a
copy of Memorandum dated 3 March,  2011
submitted by some political parties of
Haryana to the President of India regarding
misuse of the Land Acquisition Act, for
releasing farmers' land to corporate
builders; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken thereon?
Large scale cutting of trees for
POSCO Project
†*295. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
fact that large scale felling of trees is going
on the sea shore of Orissa for the proposed
POSCO Project;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether there was any mention of
such large scale felling of trees in the
agreement entered into  for establishment
of the POSCO Project;
(d) if not, whether such felling of trees
is illegal; and
(e) if so, the measures contemplated by
Government to check it?
Import of crude oil
*296. SHRI A VINASH PANDE: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the crude oil imports
from different countries of the world during
the last three financial years;
(b) whether the share of Iran in import
of crude oil, as a percentage of total
imports, has undergone any significant
change;
(c) whether there is any problem with
regard to payment for crude oil to Iranian
companies; and
(d) if so, whether Government considers
this as a reason for the change in the
quantum of crude oil imported from Iran?

89
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
NEW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 17th August, 2011 Secretary-General.
Sravana 26, 1933 (Saka)
Rural development schemes in
Chhattisgarh
†*297. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government would
expedite the approval of road construction
and other pending schemes of rural
development in Chhattisgarh keeping in
view of the conditions prevailing in the
State; and
(b) whether in view of the incidents of
blowing off of the roads and obstructing
the railway services by naxalites, there is
any plan to revive the hampered
development by curbing such activities in
consultation with the Ministry of Home
Affairs and other Ministries?
Audits of oil reserves held by ONGC
*298. SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL
DARDA: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
audits conducted by Gaffery Cline and
Associates and DeGolyer and Mac
Naughten, according to which ONGC has
64 domestic fields having a total reserve of
1.1 billion tonnes of oil and oil equivalent
natural gas;
(b) if so, by when the actual exploration,
either by the ONGC itself or through
Public-Private-Partnership entities, is
likely to be commenced; and
(c) whether any cost-benefit analysis
has been conducted so as to find out
whether ONGC's own exploration or
through auctioning of block is better and
cost-effective, keeping in view the total
scenario of timely availability?
Allotment of kerosene to Rajasthan
†*299. SHRI ASHK ALI TAK: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Rajasthan is
the largest State of the country
geographically;
(b) whether Government proposes to
increase the allotment of kerosene  from
42636 KL to 71600 KL per month, keeping
in view the geography and population of
the State; and
(c) if  not, the reasons therefor?
Augmentation of staff-strength in the
offices of Accountant-General, Kerala
300. DR. T.N. SEEMA: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Comptroller and
Auditor General (CAG) and the Central
Government have received any request from
the employees' organizations for increase
in staff strength in the offices of the
Accountant-General, Kerala (Audit), in
view of the increased work load in these
offices; and
(b) if so, whether Government will
consider the request favourably?

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Drinking Water and Sanitation :—
Environment and Forests : 286, 288, 295,
Finance : 281, 300,
Health and Family Welfare : 282, 283, 284, 287, 291,
Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises:—
Petroleum and Natural Gas : 285, 293, 296, 298, 299,
Rural Development : 289, 290, 292, 294, 297.
90
GMGIPMRND—1184RS—17-08-2011.
